authority: UNECE CEVNI Rev.6 with Corr.1 and Corr.2

briefings.title: EQUIPMENT IS NOT A LOOKOUT
briefings.body: Radar, Inland AIS and a chart display provide different kinds of information. Keep a proper lookout and check what the screen represents against the waterway and traffic.

briefings.title: NAVIGATING BY RADAR
briefings.body: Article 4.06 sets equipment and authorization conditions for navigating by radar: suitable approved radar or Inland ECDIS in navigation mode with radar overlay, a working rate-of-turn indicator where required, and a person with the specific authorization aboard.

briefings.title: RADAR TRAINING EXCEPTION
briefings.body: The authorized-person condition has a training exception for use of radar in good visibility by day or night. It does not turn a training use into unrestricted radar navigation in poor visibility.

briefings.title: SMALL CRAFT USING RADAR
briefings.body: A small craft navigating by radar needs a properly working ship-to-ship radiotelephone installation. The usual three-tone device exception for small craft does not remove the radio requirement.

briefings.title: FOLLOW A RADAR TARGET
briefings.body: Radar provides a direct target return. Article 4.06 says that when radar and Inland AIS simultaneously track a target, radar information should be considered the only reliable source for that target. Resolve a discrepancy before a close-quarters decision.

briefings.title: WHAT INLAND AIS BROADCASTS
briefings.body: Inland AIS shares vessel identity and voyage-related information such as position, speed, course and navigation status. It is a useful traffic picture, but an AIS contact may not describe every vessel or obstruction.

briefings.title: KEEP AIS DATA CURRENT
briefings.body: When AIS is required and operated, the entered data must match the vessel or convoy. Changes to dimensions, convoy type, navigation status or antenna reference point require prompt attention under Article 4.07.

briefings.title: SMALL CRAFT AIS
briefings.body: The Article 4.07 carriage requirement has exceptions for small craft, except specified police vessels equipped with radar. If a small craft uses AIS, check the equipment and radio provisions that apply; do not treat absence of an AIS target as proof of clear water.

briefings.title: RADIO NETWORKS
briefings.body: Know the locally allocated ship-to-ship, nautical-information and authority channels. Article 4.05 governs the required radiotelephone installation, readiness and use; check local requirements before entering a controlled sector.

briefings.title: REPORTING AT A BLIND SECTION
briefings.body: An equipped vessel reports on the ship-to-ship channel before a blind section, narrow channel, bridge opening or other locally designated section. Make the call early enough to inform approaching traffic.

briefings.title: SAFE SPEED IN REDUCED VISIBILITY
briefings.body: Article 6.30 requires a speed suited to reduced visibility, traffic movements and local circumstances, with necessary radiotelephone information. A small craft under way in reduced visibility also keeps a listening watch on the required channel.

briefings.title: STOP CLEAR OF THE FAIRWAY
briefings.body: If stopping because of reduced visibility, keep clear of the fairway as far as possible. Article 6.33 directs vessels not navigating by radar to the nearest safe berthing or anchoring area.

briefings.title: RADAR PASSING COORDINATION
briefings.body: An upstream vessel navigating by radar contacts oncoming traffic when it sees it or approaches a sector with unseen traffic. Give the vessel category, name, direction and position and agree on a passing procedure.

briefings.title: DOWNSTREAM DANGER
briefings.body: A downstream vessel navigating by radar must call a target presenting danger if no contact has been established, warn of the danger and agree a passing procedure. If radio contact fails, the specific Article 6.32 precautions apply.

briefings.title: A VESSEL WITHOUT RADAR IN FOG
briefings.body: A vessel not navigating by radar in reduced visibility makes for the nearest safe berth or anchorage under Article 6.33. During that passage it follows the article’s lookout, sound-signal and radio provisions as applicable.

briefings.title: FORMAL REPORTING POINTS
briefings.body: Article 8.02 sets reporting duties for specified vessel categories before designated sectors, traffic control posts, centres or locks, on the indicated channel. Sign B.11 can mark a radio requirement; local authorities can specify additional vessels.

briefings.title: REPORT CHANGES AND SECTOR PASSAGE
briefings.body: For a vessel subject to Article 8.02, give required details and report entry and exit. Report a journey interruption exceeding two hours and changed reportable data as required. Consult the local authority instructions for the precise channel and sector.

briefings.title: INFORMATION INTO DECISION
briefings.body: Before proceeding, combine direct observation, current radar and AIS data, the local radio picture and authority instructions. If visibility or equipment is inadequate, reduce speed and follow the relevant safe-berth procedure.
